sections.h2: Who does what on a St. Clair County tax bill?
sections.html:
Five county offices share the job. The Assessor estimates each parcel's value, the Board of Review decides disputes, the County Clerk works out the rate, the Treasurer mails and collects the bill, and the Clerk also runs the annual tax sale. A homeowner who needs help often has to call two of them.

The county lies directly east of St. Louis in the Metro East area, and Belleville is both the seat of government and the biggest city. Its 674 square miles (658 of them land) take in East St. Louis, O'Fallon, Fairview Heights, Mascoutah, Lebanon, Cahokia Heights, Madison and parts of Collinsville and Columbia. I-55, I-64, I-70 and I-255 cross it, 11 MetroLink stations serve it, and Scott Air Force Base lies within it. French settlers founded Cahokia in 1697, and a proclamation in 1790 created the county, the first one in what became Illinois.

Before listing, gather three items: the Treasurer's payment record for your parcel, the Assessor's property record card and a clear idea of how the year's tax will be divided at closing.

The Assessor's page lists direct lines for common errands, all through the county switchboard at 618-277-6600:

  • Tax rate questions: County Clerk, extension 2365.
  • Change of address for tax bills and assessment notices: Mapping and Platting, extension 2533.
  • Mobile home tax: Treasurer, extension 2451. Delinquent mobile home tax: County Clerk, extension 2363.

sections.h2: How do St. Clair County housing numbers compare inside the county?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 250,708 residents for July 1, 2025, compared with 257,400 counted in 2020. Midpoint value for an owned home is $180,300, with rent at $1,090 for a typical unit, and 68.4% of homes have an owner living in them. Half of households earn more than $73,854, and 12.7% of residents are below the poverty line (QuickFacts, 2020-2024).

Owning costs $1,645 a month at the midpoint for mortgage holders and $645 for owners with no loan. The county has 100,846 households averaging 2.47 people. Treat these as county-wide markers and look at actual sales near your own address.

sections.h2: When do St. Clair County property tax installments fall due?
sections.html:
Each year's tax is billed in the following year and paid in two installments. The Treasurer's schedule for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 appears below, with the office noting that every date was tentative. All of those dates are behind us, so the Treasurer can supply the schedule for the next bill.

St. Clair County Treasurer schedule, 2025 taxes payable in 2026
StepDate
First installment dueJuly 1, 2026
Second installment dueSeptember 1, 2026
Final payment before the saleOctober 30, 2026
Annual tax saleNovember 2, 2026

Source: St. Clair County Treasurer, Collection Dates. The Treasurer also set a September 18 deadline to avoid newspaper publication. Electronic payment stops at 3 p.m. on that day and on the final payment day, and a postmark earns no grace.

sections.h2: What does a late or unpaid bill cost in St. Clair County?
sections.html:
A late installment picks up a state-set penalty of 1.5% of what remains unpaid, and another 1.5% is added every thirty days. The coupon on your bill prints the amount owed with penalty. Only the Treasurer's office accepts partial payments, since collector banks refuse them.

The county can sell the lien on a parcel with unpaid tax. A homeowner whose property is the principal dwelling, with no more than six apartments, can redeem for two and one-half years, while owners of other property get two years. To redeem, the owner pays the tax plus penalties and interest, and skipping redemption can end in loss of the property. If you are selling, clear any balance at closing.

  • An escrow account does not shift responsibility. The Treasurer says the owner answers for the bill whatever the bank or servicer arranged.
  • The Treasurer does not report to credit bureaus, so a late bill does not touch your score.
  • Pay by mail, in person, at listed collector banks through the second due date, or online. Cards cost 2.5% with a $2.00 minimum.

sections.h2: How can an owner contest a St. Clair County assessment?
sections.html:
Start by reading your bill and the Assessor's property record card, looking for missing exemptions and wrong facts about the house. The Assessor measures a home's outside perimeter for square footage, so your interior measurement will be smaller. Assessed value equals one-third of estimated market value, and the estimate rests on recent sales of similar homes.

Still unhappy after talking to the Assessor? The elected three-member Board of Review sits at 10 Public Square, Belleville, IL 62220. The 30-day filing period starts once the Assessor revises assessments. Useful evidence includes a photo of your house, photos and property record cards for three comparable homes, or a recent appraisal, sales contract, settlement statement or deed. The Board's office must have your papers five days or more ahead of the hearing, or the assessment is upheld as is. A further appeal goes to the Illinois Property Tax Appeal Board.

A separate route, the Tax Objection Complaint, goes through the Circuit Clerk. It mostly serves rate disputes and is due within 75 days after the second installment date.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and deferrals can reduce a St. Clair County bill?
sections.html:
Homeowners can claim the general homestead exemption for an owner-occupied residence, and veterans, returning veterans and people with disabilities have separate ones. The county posts three senior programs on its Treasurer page.

  • Senior homestead exemption: takes $5,000 off the assessed value of a home owned and lived in by someone 65 or older.
  • Senior assessment freeze: locks the assessed value for qualifying owners. The Assessor, at 618-825-2704, sends the application.
  • Senior tax deferral: the state pays the tax and records a lien, then recovers it with 6% annual interest when the home is sold or transferred. Plan for repayment at closing if the owner used it. The Treasurer, at 618-825-2440, supplies the forms.

The Treasurer also runs a monthly payment plan for current-tax homeowners who hold the homeowner occupied exemption. Sign-up begins in August and payments start in September, with no change to the due dates.

sections.h2: How is the tax split when a St. Clair County house sells?
sections.html:
Tax arrives a year behind the period it covers, so the closing statement hands the buyer a credit for the months the seller held the house. The Assessor's staff tell owners to look in their closing papers for that proportionate share.

Pull the Treasurer's record for the parcel first, and find out whether the newest bill is paid, open or already sold. Estate houses, rentals and empty properties are the likeliest to have a delinquency. For a tax sale question, phone the County Clerk at 618-277-6600. For an exemption question, phone the Board of Review at 618-825-2489.

Put the parcel number, the latest bill and your exemption paperwork in one folder. Any buyer, cash or financed, will ask for them.

faqs.q: How many installments does St. Clair County collect, and when?
faqs.a: Two a year. The Treasurer's list for 2025 taxes payable in 2026 gave July 1 and September 1, marked tentative. The Treasurer can confirm the dates for your next bill.

faqs.q: How fast does a late St. Clair County bill grow?
faqs.a: At 1.5% of the balance every month, a rate set by the state. The coupon on your bill shows the total with penalty.

faqs.q: When must I file a St. Clair County assessment appeal?
faqs.a: Inside 30 days of the Assessor's revised assessments, with the Board of Review. A rate challenge through the Circuit Clerk runs on a separate 75-day clock from the second installment date.

faqs.q: Can a St. Clair County owner get the house back after a tax sale?
faqs.a: Yes, by redeeming. A principal dwelling with six or fewer apartments gets two and one-half years and other property two years, at the price of the tax plus penalties and interest.

faqs.q: Which St. Clair County office should a senior call for tax relief?
faqs.a: Start with the Treasurer, 618-825-2440, for deferral forms and the Assessor, 618-825-2704, for the freeze. If the $5,000 senior homestead exemption is missing from your bill, call the Board of Review, 618-825-2489.
